review_notes:
I read the whole file (lines 1–86). I also read the declarations it depends on in the Probability folder. RectifiablePath is an abbrev for a subtype of C(PathTime, X) with BoundedVariationOn γ univ. pathLengthFunction is a StieltjesFunction built from variationOnFromTo. pathLengthMeasure is that function's .measure. All three are built from Mathlib's StieltjesFunction and variation API and are not competing definitions.

The new declarations in this file are pathLengthMeasure_le_of_interval_bounds, lipschitzMappedPath and lipschitzMappedPath_length_le. The first and third are theorems, which are outside this rubric. lipschitzMappedPath is a bundled map on the project's own rectifiable-path subtype. It uses Mathlib's LipschitzOnWith.comp_boundedVariationOn and ContinuousOn.comp_continuous, so it does not reimplement anything. Mathlib's Path and Path.map are different (endpoint-fixed, no bounded-variation constraint), so they do not replace it.

I found no independent competing concept and no concrete cost from duplication, so I abstain. The only uncertainty is that I did not search all of Mathlib for a pre-existing bounded-variation path subtype. I judged that unlikely to exist.
